title: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases
summary: Taking off a protective case shouldn't double as a teardown.
content: TL;DR The removable back panels on the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite can accidentally detach when removing a protective case. The issue occurs even with Amazon’s official cover, but hasn’t been observed on the aluminum Kindle or Paperwhite Signature Edition. Amazon says owners can simply press the panel back into place, although reassembly can cause alignment issues. We got our first hint that Amazon was preparing to make Kindle batteries easier to replace back in May, and the company delivered on that front with the launch of its redesigned Kindle lineup in October. It’s a welcome change for devices that people often keep for years, but some owners of the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite are discovering that the removable back panel can come loose long before it’s time for a new battery. A Kindle owner on Reddit demonstrated how their Ube Kindle comes apart when removing a protective case. TikTok creator Jackie’s Book Tally shared a similar experience, showing how trying to peel away a clear case to put some stickers on the back of her Kindle causes the device’s housing to separate.

title: ANBERNIC’s next Snapdragon-powered Game Boy-like handheld comes with active cooling

It will also pack in the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chipset, which we’ve seen on the ANBERNIC RG 55G1 , and a 5,500mAh battery with an active cooling system. The teaser also showcases the handheld in three colors: Pika Yellow, Retro Purple, and Black.

title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
summary: Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.
content: TL;DR Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals. According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.

If you’re fond of ChatGPT and prefer it over Gemini , you can already assign it as the default assistant on your Android devices . But now, OpenAI could be working on giving ChatGPT more control on your Android device — with your permission. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. title: Gemini ran my errands on the Pixel 10 like I was in a sci-fi movie
summary: Want to spend your time watching Gemini use your phone?
content: Gemini Intelligence isn’t just a marketing term that Google slaps onto its Pixel phones. It enables a bunch of handy AI features, including task automation — the dream use case for artificial intelligence. A whole bouquet of these automations recently made their way t o last year’s Pixel 10 in newer regions, after debuting on the Pixel 11, and I couldn’t keep myself from giving it a go. Gemini can already work inside a few apps in the backend, but it can now interact with third-party apps just like you do, using the same visual interface. It brings to reality the idea of AI taking over your mundane tasks like a true assistant. After living with Gemini Intelligence on the Pixel 10, I feel like I’ve had a taste of the future.

summary: Additionally, Gemini Live could get a brand-new text box to type your request.
content: TL;DR The Google Gemini app is testing a new Activity option containing Scheduled and Tasks tabs. These two tabs should let users check on their existing one-time tasks or ones they’ve scheduled to run periodically. Google is also working on a new text box for the Gemini Live experience, with traces of this particular addition appearing a couple of months ago. Google Gemini already lets you create one-time or scheduled tasks using Gemini Live , and the app could soon let you access them more easily. We have spotted development on a new option that brings these two elements together. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. We looked into version 17.78.14 of the Google app to activate a new Activity option at the top of the Gemini Live interface, featuring tabs named Tasks and Scheduled. While we could surface both pages in our testing, neither displayed any of the tasks and scheduled actions we created.

title: Google Health won’t let users manually add rests between workout sets
summary: The Health Coach can do something the manual workout builder can't.
content: TL;DR Google Health’s manual workout builder lacks the option to schedule rests between sets, even though the Premium-exclusive Health Coach supports it. Live workout metrics can also fail to appear in the app, even with an active smartwatch connection. We’ve reached out to Google to find out whether fixes are in the works and when users can expect them. One of the biggest fitness upgrades in the November Pixel Drop lets Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 owners follow workouts directly on their wrists, with timers and audio cues that tell them when to move on to the next set or exercise. But as more users get access to step-by-step workouts , a scheduling limitation for rest between sets and a bug affecting live workout metrics are taking some of the shine off the experience. Multiple Google Health users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) report that while they can schedule rest periods between different exercises when building a custom workout, they can’t do the same between sets of an individual exercise.

title: First look: Google Play Store’s new ‘Today’ feed could pull content from your favorite apps
summary: It could make Collections even more useful.
content: TL;DR Google is working on a new “Today” feed for Collections in the Play Store. It combines recommendations from multiple apps into a single feed. Users can also choose which apps contribute content to the feed. It’s been a while since Google first introduced Collections in the Play Store , and the feature has largely remained unchanged, barring some new widgets we spotted the company working on. Although Collections is quite good at organizing content from your installed apps into separate categories, Google is now working on a new feed that brings all of these recommendations together. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. While digging through the latest version of the Google Play Store (v54.4.11), we found evidence of Google working on a new “Today” feed inside Collections. With a bit of tinkering, we managed to enable it on our device. The new tab appears right next to “App Library,” ahead of the existing content categories.

title: OnePlus 15 and 15R ColorOS 17 update adds auto PC unlocking, smarter photo storage, and more
summary: ColorOS users are catching up with their OxygenOS counterparts.
content: TL;DR OnePlus is rolling out a ColorOS 17 update to the OnePlus 15 and 15R that adds automatic PC unlocking through the O Plus Connect app. The update also lets users free up storage by removing backed-up photos, customize image quality and resolution, and connect their phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time. Both phones get Calculator, Translate, and privacy improvements, alongside the November 2026 security patch. Earlier this month, OnePlus rolled out an OxygenOS 16 update that lets your phone automatically unlock your PC when connecting remotely . ColorOS users missed out on this feature at the time, receiving translation improvements instead. That’s changing with the latest ColorOS 17 update for the OnePlus 15 and 15R , which brings automatic PC unlocking, November 2026 security patches, and several other useful additions. With the update, O Plus Connect can use a saved password to automatically unlock your computer during a remote connection, saving you the trouble of entering it manually. To set this up, tap the More icon on the floating ball during a remote connection, select Unlock PC, and enable “Automatically unlock when connected.” The update also lets you connect your phone and tablet to the same PC at the same time.

title: Oura is dropping Android 11 support in December, and users risk losing health data
summary: Upgrading after the deadline won't bring back your health history.
content: TL;DR Oura will officially drop support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. Users who don’t upgrade to Android 12 or newer by the deadline risk losing their historical health data. Those who remain on Android 11 may retain access to some limited historical app features. One of the biggest benefits of wearing an Oura Ring is that the longer you use it, the more you learn about your health. From personalized annual health recaps to long-term blood pressure trends, many of Oura’s features become more useful as you build up months or even years of health data. However, some Android users could soon lose access to that history simply because of the phone they use. Oura has updated its Android software updates support page to reveal that it will discontinue support for Android 11 on December 8, 2026. Starting on that date, you’ll need a phone running Android 12 or newer to continue enjoying the full Oura app experience.

title: Samsung Messages could soon find, send, and forward texts for you
summary: The app's development is far from over.
content: TL;DR Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 is rolling out in South Korea with groundwork for hands-free message management. The update also hints at smarter message searches and the ability to check how received photos were created or edited. Similar capabilities were spotted in China in September, but global versions of Samsung Messages still lack these additions. Samsung may have shut down its Messages app in the US in July , but that hasn’t stopped the company from developing new features for users elsewhere. The latest update rolling out in South Korea suggests Samsung is preparing its texting app for a future where AI assistants can do much more than help you write messages. As Sam Updater spotted, Samsung Messages version 16.3.27.7 introduces support for 10 functions that AI assistants such as Gemini could use to interact directly with the app. These include drafting, sending, replying to, forwarding, searching for, and deleting messages, as well as looking up contacts.

title: Samsung is building a Siri-style Vision mode for its Camera app, along with Auto portrait
summary: Both features are likely bound for the Galaxy S27 series.
content: Credit: Zac Kew-Denniss / Android Authority TL;DR Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to a new “Vision mode” in Samsung’s Camera app. It will seemingly describe what you point at and hand off follow-up questions to Gemini. The same build also points to a new “Auto portrait” feature, which could add background blur in Photo mode whenever it spots a face or a pet. Neither feature works on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, and the code suggests both need new hardware, so they will likely debut on the Galaxy S27 series. Pointing your camera at something and asking your phone about it isn’t really a new feature these days. Samsung shipped Bixby Vision with the Galaxy S8 back in 2017. Google has Lens and Circle to Search, and Gemini Live’s camera sharing has been on Android phones since last year. Apple was late to the party with Visual Intelligence . Then, with iOS 27, Apple moved Visual Intelligence to the Camera app , where a new Siri mode lives alongside Photo, Video, and other camera modes. Despite beating Apple to the punch, Samsung appears to be preparing its own refreshed version of this feature, seemingly borrowing from Apple’s UX. We dug through the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s One UI 9.5 Beta 1 firmware and found a new Vision mode in the Camera app, plus an Auto portrait feature for Photo mode.

title: We tested Samsung’s private Galaxy AI cloud on One UI 9.5 beta, and it made AI select smarter
summary: Running AI select through Samsung SPAC on a Galaxy S26 Ultra produced an accurate calendar entry that didn't need edits.
content: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR We got Samsung’s private AI cloud, referred to as “SPAC” in the code, working with AI select on a Galaxy S26 Ultra running One UI 9.5 Beta 1, producing more accurate calendar event extraction than its standard processing. Code references show SPAC supports Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6 (used in our test) and appears to route encrypted requests through a third-party relay to hide user identity. In our test, SPAC only pulled one event out of the five listed, but Samsung’s code indicates multi-event support. It also suggests photo editing, live translation, and writing tools could adopt SPAC next. Yesterday, we reported that Samsung is building a private cloud for Galaxy AI . The system, called “SPAC” in Samsung’s code, appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute . At the time, SPAC wasn’t switched on for our Galaxy S26 Ultra. Now we’ve managed to get it running, and the result is better than what Galaxy AI does today. APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship. AI select used SPAC to add an event to our calendar AI select, part of the Samsung Capture app, can pull details from your screen and suggest actions, like adding an event to your calendar. We pointed it at a Google search result listing upcoming Lollapalooza dates and tapped “Add event.”

title: TCL CSOT unveils APEX and IJP OLED breakthroughs for the AI era at DTC 2026
summary: TCL CSOT showed off the future of display tech at DTC 2026.
content: Credit: TCL CSOT A screen has a big impact on how a device feels to use. It determines how crisp text looks on your laptop, how smoothly fast-moving games appear on your monitor, how long your phone lasts on a charge, and whether the person next to you on the train can read your screen. OLED screens, in particular, need a lot of precision to manufacture, which is why they’re most often found only in higher-end phones, laptops, monitors, and tablets. TCL CSOT, which makes and develops displays for many device manufacturers, is working on a method to build OLED panels by printing the materials onto them, which could help OLED get into more products.

title: Got a MediaTek, Exynos, or Pixel device? Here are 11 tips for emulation
summary: From specific settings to alternative emulators, here's what you can try on your non-Snapdragon device.
content: Credit: Nick Fernandez / Android Authority There’s no shortage of emulators on Android , letting you play everything from Atari 2600 and NES games to PC and Nintendo Switch titles. We’ve even seen Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Switch 2 emulators in recent times. It’s fair to say, though, that devices with Qualcomm Snapdragon chips are generally the best for emulation. Phones and handhelds with MediaTek, Google Tensor, or Samsung Exynos silicon often suffer from worse performance and compatibility with new emulators as a result. Thankfully, there are plenty of tips you can try if you’re struggling with emulation on your MediaTek-powered device, Exynos-toting Galaxy phone, or Google Pixel.

But much like other consumer electronics, it was affected by the AI-induced RAM crisis.

title: Morphe v2.4.0 beats Google to bringing YouTube videos to your Android Auto screen
summary: It only shows up when your vehicle is parked.
content: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Morphe v2.4.0 is out, and it adds support for playing YouTube videos on Android Auto and other in-car entertainment platforms. YouTube shows up in the Android Auto launcher when the car is parked. Along with this, Morphe’s version of YouTube and YouTube Music also get a host of playability improvements. Morphe is a popular open-source tool for modding popular Android apps to add features and remove ads from YouTube, YouTube Music, and other media streaming apps. In the last major update, it added 4K video downloads , surpassing download-quality limits even on the official YouTube app. Now, it’s out with another update that brings a host of changes to patched versions of Reddit, YouTube, and YouTube Music. One that truly stands out — and we hope isn’t blocked by Google — is the ability to play YouTube videos on Android Auto. Release notes for version 2.40 of the Morphe app say a new patch now lets Morphe YouTube be seen as a “parked video app.” As a result, the app shows up in Android Auto’s app drawer, and you can watch videos directly while your vehicle isn’t moving. This is currently only available as an early access feature and also works with DriveDeck. Google itself has been working to bring a similar functionality to phones running Android 17 or newer by the end of the year. Currently, users can only listen to audio from YouTube videos on Android Auto , but the app must be controlled from the phone.
